Middle East.headline: 130,000 Displaced: Yemen’s Refugee Crisis reaches Somalia
Middle East.body: Yemen’s truce is over and people are already crossing the Gulf of Aden. A refugee crisis is starting on the Somali coast, in places already stretched past their limits. In early September, Ansarullah, the de facto government of most of Yemen, known in the Western Press as “the Houthis”, launched against Yemen’s “internationally recognised” government. Ansarullah runs northern Yemen (the most densely populated part of the country). It took Mocha on 10 September and Mayyun (Perim) Island the next day, . It now holds , and its forces are . Shipping has already thinned. Crossings fell to fifteen in a single day, and tankers carried about 5.2 million barrels a day through the strait, down from 8.

Middle East.headline: Pakistani Driver reportedly killed in Drone Strike on Aid Truck in Yemen
Middle East.body: SANAA – Yemeni government forces accused Houthis of carrying out drone strike on an aid truck traveling to Marib province, reportedly killing Pakistani driver. There has been no immediate statement from Pakistani authorities regarding the reported incident. First confirmed Pakistani casualty in Yemen: A Houthi drone struck a relief truck in Marib, #Yemen, killing a Pakistani driver. This comes after a Pakistani official claimed dispatching four cargo aircraft carrying military equipment and aid to government-held areas of Yemen. Americas.headline: Haiti: UN chief condemns Haiti attack that killed 47
Americas.body: At least 47 people, including at least five children, were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped by armed men in Haiti on Sunday, the United Nations confirmed on Tuesday. The incident, which took place in Kenscoff on the outskirts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in the troubled Caribbean country in recent years. In a video posted on social media, a gang leader threatened to murder hostages if Haiti's National Police kill any of his men in an attempt to rescue people. "If any of our soldiers are hurt, I will kill all of them," he said.

Americas.headline: El Niño Threatens 347 Million Children as Floods and Droughts Put Their Futures at Risk
Americas.body: Devdiscourse News Desk | New York For millions of children, the approaching El Niño could mean losing access to drinking water, missing school or leaving home because floods or drought have made everyday life unsafe. The 2026–2027 event is forecast to become one of the strongest on record, with UNICEF warning that more than 347 million children across nearly 100 countries and territories live in areas expected to experience unusually wet or dry conditions between October and December 2026. Americas.headline: New Data Reveals Nearly 1.5 Million Displaced In Haiti As Instability Escalates
Americas.body: As armed gangs continue to act as de facto authorities in Haiti, recent reports reveal that approximately 12 percent of the population, roughly 1.5 million Haitians, are now displaced, according to data collected by the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Additionally, 80 percent of people being displaced are located outside of Port-au-Prince, Haiti’s capital and largest city, with the most significant increase recorded in Haiti’s Artibonite department, a rural northern region, where displacement rose by 16 percent between May and August 2026, according to the IOM. Americas.headline: In 2010 Haiti was devastated by a 7.0-magnitude earthquake: Just hours later, Sean Penn...
Americas.body: Haiti is no stranger to hardship and suffering. The Caribbean island nation is especially vulnerable to natural disasters given its location. It is prone to being pummeled by tropical cyclones, massive flooding events, and major earthquakes. On 12 January 2010, Haiti was struck by a 7.0 earthquake shortly before 5 pm local time that killed 220,000 people, one of the deadliest in recorded history. It also left around 1.5 million people homeless. Aid organizations and emergency crews rushed to Haiti to provide much needed relief and resources. Africa.headline: UN condemns deadly airstrike on marked aid trucks in Sudan amid humanitarian crisis
Africa.body: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) on Monday condemned a deadly airstrike on two trucks delivering aid in South Kordofan state, Sudan, which resulted in the death of one of the drivers. According to the WFP, the attack occurred in the early hours of Saturday, when two trucks clearly marked as humanitarian vehicles were transporting food and other commodities to civilians in South Kordofan. The organisation did not provide any further details about the circumstances of the airstrike or the extent of damage to the food cargo, which are under assessment. Europe.headline: At least 6 dead as Russia strikes Ukraine’s Kharkiv
Europe.body: At least 6 people have been killed in Ukraine's northeastern city of Kharkiv after a Russian strike hit a residential area. Nearly 60 were injured and apartments destroyed. Elsewhere, a Russian drone struck an apartment building in the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia. Morgan Ayre has the details.

Europe.headline: Ship sinks and crew missing after Black Sea drone attack
Europe.body: Ship sinks and crew missing after Black Sea drone attack. It is not clear who is behind the attacks which come as Russia intensifies strikes in the Black Sea as part of its war against Ukraine.

Europe.headline: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks
Europe.body: - Published Ukraine's railways have kept the country running since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. But attacks are intensifying, with more than half of all strikes on locomotives since then occurring this year alone, according to the state-owned operator. Europe.headline: Plague epidemic risk in Russia low after death of lab technician, WHO says
Europe.body: World Health Organization detects no sign of further outbreak since Darya Shipilova died last week The World Health Organization has said the risk of an epidemic in Russia is lowafter the sudden death of a lab technician who worked at a plague research institute in Siberia. Darya Shipilova, who was 28, died last week, two days after falling ill. Russian media reports suggested she may have become infected after an accident at her workplace , where dangerous pathogens are kept and studied. Continue reading...

Asia-Pacific.headline: At Least 8 Dead in Myanmar Air Strikes, Rakhine Rebel Group Claims
Asia-Pacific.body: Myanmar’s military has launched airstrikes on camps for internally displaced people in Rakhine State, killing at least eight people and leaving more injured, according to a local ethnic rebel organization. The Arakan Army (AA), a Rakhine nationalist group that controls much of the state in western Myanmar, said yesterday that a Y12 aircraft bombed a displacement shelter and a nearby village in AA-controlled Ponnagyun Township, The Irrawaddy reported. One civilian was killed and two injured in the attack, it added. This came after six were killed in an air attack on a separate displacement camp in the township on Sunday night, the AA claimed. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ebola disease outbreak spreads like a megafire in North Kivu as new hotspots multiply
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Ebola disease outbreak in North Kivu province, Democratic Republic of Congo, has intensified dramatically since early September, with the province now accounting for nearly 40 per cent of all newly confirmed cases nationwide. This is up from 24 per cent at the end of August. With new hotspots emerging every week, treatment capacities remain largely insufficient and inadequate. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ebola outbreak shows that the world is not ready for the next pandemic
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: As Ebola continues to spread in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the burning question at recent UN pandemic preparedness meetings at the UN General Assembly was: Is the world willing and able to pay for readiness? When the Marburg virus hit Rwanda in September 2024, the country’s No. 1 goal was stopping community transmission. Marburg, in the same family as the Ebola virus, is second among the top-four deadliest viruses in the world. More than 80 per cent of people who contract the disease die. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Angola engages media at health center to fight Mpox outbreak - APAnews
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Angolan government has intensified its national risk communication strategy by hosting media professionals at the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (COESP) in Luanda to strengthen public access to reliable information surrounding the ongoing Mpox outbreak. Against the backdrop of 796 confirmed cases and two recorded fatalities across the country since 2024, the initiative brought journalists from diverse media organizations directly into the operational heart of Angola’s epidemiological response.
